target.title: fix(agents): proxy SSE idle cancel rejection can replace stall error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a rejecting `reader.cancel()` during proxy SSE idle timeout cleanup could surface as an unhandled rejection (or compete with the stall error). The same file already swallows cancel failures on the pending-buffer overflow path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Match the local sibling at the pending-buffer cancel site: `void reader.cancel(...).catch(() => undefined)` so idle-timeout cleanup stays best-effort and the stall error remains authoritative.

## User Impact

**Before:** Idle SSE cancel rejection could become an unhandled rejection while the stream was already failing for stall.

**After:** Cancel rejection is swallowed; the stream still fails with the SSE stall error; process emits zero `unhandledRejection` events for that cancel failure.

## Evidence

### Proof (exit 0)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts -t "keeps the SSE idle stall error|returns an error result when the SSE read idles" --reporter=verbose
```

```text
stdout | ../../src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts > streamProxy > keeps the SSE idle stall error when reader.cancel rejects
[proxy sse idle cancel-reject proof] stall_preserved=true cancel_called=true unhandled_rejections=0 errorMessage=Proxy SSE stream stalled: no data received for 120000ms

 ✓ |agents-core| ../../src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts > streamProxy > returns an error result when the SSE read idles 280ms
 ✓ |agents-core| ../../src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts > streamProxy > keeps the SSE idle stall error when reader.cancel rejects 4ms
 ✓ |agents-support| ../../src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts > streamProxy > returns an error result when the SSE read idles 330ms
 ✓ |agents-support| ../../src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts > streamProxy > keeps the SSE idle stall error when reader.cancel rejects 10ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  4 passed | 26 skipped (30)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Proxy SSE idle timeout still reports stall when `reader.cancel` rejects, with no process-level `unhandledRejection`.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `streamProxy` → `readProxySseChunk` idle timer → `reader.cancel(timeoutError).catch(...)` → stall error result.
- **Boundary crossed:** ReadableStream cancel rejection → swallowed; stall `errorMessage` preserved; `unhandledRejections` array stays empty after microtask flush.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Same `.catch(() => undefined)` pattern as pending-buffer cancel in the same file (#111105/#111106 family).
- **Observed result after fix:** `stall_preserved=true cancel_called=true unhandled_rejections=0` with stall errorMessage (see proof log).
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

target.title: fix(models): make nested modelPolicy wildcards match by segment boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow` accepts wildcard entries, but a **nested-namespace** wildcard such as `clawrouter/anthropic/*` matched *nothing*. Only a single trailing segment was ever compared, so a provider/vendor-scoped allow entry silently locked out every model it was meant to permit — the operator's allowlist looked valid but denied all traffic. There was also no validation, so empty, bare, or malformed refs were accepted and simply mis-behaved at runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

Model policy refs are hierarchical (`provider/vendor/model`, arbitrary depth). Wildcard matching must respect segment boundaries at every depth: `clawrouter/anthropic/*` should allow `clawrouter/anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` but must reject `clawrouter/google/...`, `openai/...`, and a sibling like `clawrouter/anthropicX/...`. The prior single-segment comparison couldn't express that, and each consumer (enforcement, catalog visibility, picker, `models status`) rolled its own partial logic, so they disagreed.

This introduces one canonical parser/matcher (`src/config/model-policy-ref.ts`) and routes every consumer through it, plus config-time validation that rejects malformed refs while preserving opaque nested model IDs from dynamic providers.

## User Impact

- Nested wildcards now work: `clawrouter/anthropic/*` permits exactly the models under that prefix and nothing else. Top-level wildcards (`clawrouter/*`) are unchanged.
- `openclaw models status --json` `.allowed` reports the concrete matching catalog models instead of echoing the raw wildcard string.
- Malformed policy refs (empty, bare, bad segment/wildcard) are rejected at config validation with a clear error, instead of silently denying all models at runtime.
- No change to existing valid single-segment or top-level policies.

## Evidence

- Canonical ref parse/match: `src/config/model-policy-ref.ts`; segment-boundary enforcement `src/agents/model-selection-shared.ts`.
- Consumers unified: catalog visibility (`model-catalog-visibility.ts`), directive handling (`directive-handling.model.ts`), status (`commands/models/list.status-command.ts`).
- Validation: `src/config/validation.ts` rejects malformed refs, preserves opaque nested model IDs.
- 249 focused tests pass (17 policy, 122 selection, 35 picker, 29 status, 46 validation). Build passed. AutoReview `--mode branch --base origin/main`: patch is correct (0.86).
- Live gateway proof (isolated, port 18899): `clawrouter/anthropic/*` allowed an Anthropic ClawRouter turn, rejected a Google ClawRouter turn *before* upstream, and `models status` reported only `clawrouter/anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` as allowed.
